title: packaging: NSIS: Fix profile paths with spaces on MinGW cross-compile
description:
cmake_path(NATIVE_PATH ...) and file(TO_NATIVE_PATH ...) use the
build system path style, not the target system. For NSIS packaging,
the source file location directives (File) are processed when building
the package, but the OutPath is processed when actually installing, so
the former needs to be in the build system path but the latter in the
target (Windows) path style.

In addition, file(TO_NATIVE_PATH ...) escapes spaces in paths with
a backslash, whereas cmake_path(NATIVE_PATH ...) does not. (This does
not appear to be documented.) The backslash escape causes problems
when running the nsis package command under MinGW, which attempts to
autodetect UN*X vs Windows paths and convert them, but has problems
with backslash escapes. We quote the path, so the escape is not needed.

We already require CMake 3.20, where cmake_path was introduced (and the
file(...) native path conversion was apparently deprecated.)

https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/5939
https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/command/cmake_path.html#native-conversion
https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/command/file.html#path-conversion

Prevent issues like:

File: "/home/johnthacker/wireshark/resources/share/wireshark/profiles/No\ Reassembly/preferences" -> no files found.
Usage: File [/nonfatal] [/a] ([/r] [/x filespec [...]] filespec [...] |
   /oname=outfile one_file_only)
!include: error in script: "/home/johnthacker/wireshark-builds/wireshark-mingw-build/packaging/nsis/wireshark-profile-manifest.nsh" on line 8
Error in script "wireshark.nsi" on line 1131 -- aborting creation process
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.

Fix #21022

See e4ce183215f9b1369ea3b234814b747978a3cddf

AI-Assisted: no

changes_data.diff:
@@ -186,10 +186,21 @@ if (BUILD_wireshark)
 		if(${_profile_file} MATCHES "^([^/]+)/.+")
 			if (NOT ${_outdir} STREQUAL ${CMAKE_MATCH_1})
 				set(_outdir "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
+				# file and cmake_path use the format of the
+				# build system, not target system, so using
+				# NATIVE_PATH won't work when cross-compiling.
+				# The OutPath is parsed by the installing
+				# system.
 				set(_profile_manifest_contents "${_profile_manifest_contents}SetOutPath '\$INSTDIR\\profiles\\${_outdir}'\n")
 			endif()
-			file(TO_NATIVE_PATH "${_profile_file}" _native_profile_file)
-			set(_profile_manifest_contents "${_profile_manifest_contents}File \"\${TOP_SRC_DIR}\\resources\\share\\wireshark\\profiles\\${_native_profile_file}\"\n")
+			# Using a UN*X style path still works when finding the
+			# source file to add when cross-compiling, because that
+			# is done on the build system. file(TO_NATIVE_PATH ...)
+			# adds an escaping backslash before a space on MinGW,
+			# which won't work, but cmake_path(NATIVE_PATH ...)
+			# doesn't, so use the latter.
+			cmake_path(CONVERT "${TOP_SRC_DIR}/resources/share/wireshark/profiles/${_profile_file}" TO_NATIVE_PATH_LIST _native_profile_file)
+			set(_profile_manifest_contents "${_profile_manifest_contents}File \"${_native_profile_file}\"\n")
 		endif()
 	endforeach()
 	file(WRITE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/wireshark-profile-manifest.nsh" "${_profile_manifest_contents}")
@@ -240,8 +251,8 @@ if (BUILD_stratoshark)
 				set(_outdir "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
 				set(_profile_manifest_contents "${_profile_manifest_contents}SetOutPath '\$INSTDIR\\profiles\\${_outdir}'\n")
 			endif()
-			file(TO_NATIVE_PATH "${_profile_file}" _native_profile_file)
-			set(_profile_manifest_contents "${_profile_manifest_contents}File \"\${TOP_SRC_DIR}\\resources\\share\\stratoshark\\profiles\\${_native_profile_file}\"\n")
+			cmake_path(CONVERT "${TOP_SRC_DIR}/resources/share/stratoshark/profiles/${_profile_file}" TO_NATIVE_PATH_LIST _native_profile_file)
+			set(_profile_manifest_contents "${_profile_manifest_contents}File \"${_native_profile_file}\"\n")
 		endif()
 	endforeach()
 	file(WRITE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/stratoshark-profile-manifest.nsh" "${_profile_manifest_contents}")
